channel.title: Comments for page "I'll See You Next Time"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "I'll See You Next Time"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is the third sad tale in a row from the random tale dispenser.

A lot of the comments mention how making 055 a person is a very boring choice, but I disagree. It really makes you think about what an existence like that would be, and the character is pretty well-written.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This does not work for me.

055 is unknowable in the same way that 682 is unkillable. Works that circumvent that central and essential element of their respective natures need to be amazing just to avoid being awful, because they're not really expansions on the source material, they're de facto rewrites of it. To kill 682 or reveal 055, a merely good story is insufficient.

-1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I can accept 55 as a person, fits as well as anything else does.
And I kind of like the effective immortality because of a body that "forgets" to starve or age.
But that only works if she is not immune to the anomaly.
And if she is not immune, how does she remember the interviews? Tyler forgets, I can see no fridge-logic for why she wouldn't.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: One of the acceptable interpretations of the contest is how a SCP changes over time. In this case, if I'm reading it correctly, 055 is thinking about how Time has forgotten her, like everything else. How, when no-one remembers her, interactions with other people become almost like a time loop because they don't remember what they did last time and repeat it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While I like it, I don't really see how time was incoporated. A nice backstory, but it doesn't really concern time at all. It's like I can walk up to 055 right now and the story would be exactly the same.

Like it as a tale, not as a contest entry. Probably would upvote after the contest is over.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Have you had any significant incidents with our personnel?

What do you mean?

Why?

This batch of questions doesn't make particular sense, given that they don't really know what 055 will respond. I would think they'd just trust the agent to ask for a clarification in case of any interesting answers.

This piece kind of bores me. Once you get that it's 055 (which I was spoiled with going in), there's little beyond the obvious.

I have a neutral opinion of this piece. Probably because you chose SCP-055. Considering the infinite possibility involved with that kind of anomaly, you went in an awfully vanilla direction with it.

It's okay, though. I can see where it would be liked. And it's technically sound. So, I'm not going to minus you.

Still… meh.
